paper.title: Online Learning of Halfspaces with Massart Noise

settings.name_in_paper: Online Learning with Massart Noise (gamma-margin halfspaces)
unmapped: Online binary classification: the learner predicts a label in {+1,-1} for an adversarially chosen point x_t in the unit ball and suffers 0-1 loss
Labels follow a Massart noise model: Pr[y_t != sign(w*.x_t) | x_t] <= eta for an unknown unit vector w*
Adversary's points have geometric margin |w*.x_t| >= gamma
The learner knows the noise rate eta and the margin gamma (used to set Delta~ = 1-2eta-eps and tau = eps*gamma/4)
settings.definition_quote: Fix a class of concepts $\mathcal C$ over $\R^d$ and a target concept $c^\ast \in \mathcal C$. At round $t = 1,\ldots, T$: The adversary selects a point $\x^{(t)} \in \R^d$ and generates a random label $y^{(t)}$ such that $\pr[y^{(t)} \neq c^\ast(\x^{(t)}) \mid \x^{(t)} ] \leq \eta$. The learner observes $\x^{(t)}$, predicts a label $\hat y^{(t)}$, and suffers loss $\1\{\hat y^{(t)} \neq y^{(t)}\}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual Bandits with Monotone Rewards (Massart Bandits)
unmapped: Each round the adversary picks k contexts x_1..x_k in the unit ball and a reward distribution on [0,M]^k that may change with t and the context
Semi-parametric monotone reward model: if w*.x_i > w*.x_j then E[r_i - r_j] >= Delta (reward margin), for an unknown unit vector w*
Geometric margin: |w*.x_i - w*.x_j| >= gamma for all i != j
The learner knows the reward margin Delta and geometric margin gamma (used to tune Lambda and q)
settings.definition_quote: Fix some unit vector $\vec w^\ast \in \R^d$, $\gamma, \Delta, M > 0$, and a class of monotone reward distributions $\D$. At round $t$: The adversary picks context $\matr X^{(t)} \in \mathcal{X}$ and draws a random reward vector $\vec r\tth$ from $D^{(t, \matr X\tth)}$. The learner observes the context $\matr X^{(t)}$, picks action $a^{(t)} \in [K]$ and receives reward $\vec r_{a^{(t)}}$.

algorithms.name: Online Learning Massart Halfspaces (Algorithm 1: OGD on margin-reweighted LeakyReLU loss)

symbols.eta: Massart noise rate (upper bound on label flip probability)
symbols.gamma: geometric margin of the adversary's points w.r.t. w*

conditions: |w*.x_t| >= gamma for all t, for some unit vector w*
tuning: Delta~ = 1-2eta-eps, tau = Theta(eps^(1+zeta) gamma), eps = Theta(T^(-1/(4+2zeta))/gamma), OGD step size D/(G sqrt(T))

source.label: thm:2-arm
source.quote: Consider the Online Massart Learning setting of \Cref{def:online-massart}. Additionally, assume that the examples picked by the adversary have at least $\gamma$-margin with respect to some target halfpsace, i.e., for all $t=1,\ldots, T$, it holds that $\|\x^{(t)}\|_2 \leq 1$ and $|\vec w^\ast \cdot \x^{(t)}| \geq \gamma$, for some unit vector $\vec w^\ast$. There exists an algorithm that does $M(T) = \eta T + O(T^{3/4}/\gamma)$ mistakes and runs in $\poly(d)$ time per round.

results.notes: Quantity is the expected number of mistakes M(T) (not regret); only the T^{3/4}/gamma term is inside O(.) in the paper, eta*T has coefficient 1. Proof actually gives T^{3/4-O(zeta)} for zeta -> 0, somewhat informal.

symbols.Delta_r: reward margin: E[r_i - r_j] >= Delta_r whenever w*.x_i > w*.x_j

conditions: |w*.x_i - w*.x_j| >= gamma for all i != j, for some unit vector w*
reward distributions monotone w.r.t. w* with margin Delta_r (Definition 1.4)

source.label: thm:bandit
source.quote: There exists a bandit algorithm that runs in $\poly(d)$ time per round and selects a sequence of arms $\alpha^{(1)}, \ldots, \alpha^{(T)} \in [k]$ that obtain expected reward \E\left[\sum_{t=1}^T \vec r\tth(\alpha\tth) \right] \geq \E\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^k \vec r_i\tth\right] +\frac{k-1}{k}\Delta T - O(T^{5/6}(k \Delta M^2)^{1/3}/\gamma)

results.notes: Recorded quantity: shortfall of the learner's expected reward relative to (uniform-random reward + (k-1)/k * Delta * T), which is at most the stated expression. Not a standard regret. Corollary 1.11 (k=2) is the special case with the same expression; not recorded separately. Restated as Theorem A.5.
